newsitem.title: USA: Infoseek to launch advertising network.
newsitem.headline: Infoseek to launch advertising network.

text.p: Infoseek Corp is expected Monday to launch a network for selling advertising on third party Internet sites to reduce the cost and difficulty of selling advertisement inventory on the World Wide Web.

The company, which went public in June and runs a free, advertising-supported Internet navigation service, is aiming its new line of business at advertisers seeking to target consumers on destination sites as well as its search engine.
Infoseek Network also aims to help fill a large portion of the available advertising inventory on Web sites that remain unsold despite the popularity of the new medium.

Internet analysts have noted that large Web sites such as those run by Infoseek and its rivals, such as Yahoo Corp as well as other advertising-based Web sites only sell a portion of the possible advertising space.

Yahoo executives last week, for example, said that although its site averaged some 14 million hits a day in the month of September, or roughly 50 percent of the traffic on the commercial, advertising-supported search engines, only about a quarter of its pages delivered included advertising.

Infoseek is expected to offer advertisers the ability to place ads on some of the most frequently visited Internet sites and to use its own advertising delivery system to enable advertisers to target specific audiences.
Infoseek officials said its remote ad delivery system is currently in beta testing and is delivering ads to more than 20 sites across the Internet.

To become an Infoseek Network affiliate, sites must generate a minimum of 300,000 impressions a month and also meet with requirements for quality and subject matter. The company also is expected to extend the network to Japan.
